To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of BPS tools can facilitate the conceptual design process by providing the facilities to (1) explore the option space; (2) quantify parameter interactions; (3) generate and evaluate design alternatives; and (4) quantify the accuracy of the simulation results.
The integration of uncertainty and sensitivity analysis techniques into BPS tools for conceptual building design is beneficial for designers to support decision making.

(1) BPS tools have the potential of supporting conceptual design, (2) BPS tools need to be flexible in their interfaces to adapt to the different levels of abstraction and (3) BPS tools can be extended with techniques for uncertainty analysis to support decision making.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of tools that support the design process and that are capable to provide quantitative information regarding the uncertainty of performance predictions and their sensitivities to design changes.
the use of BPS tools to support conceptual design and to provide the necessary information to make design decisions.
the development of a simulation tool that provides a means to quantify the uncertainty of performance predictions and sensitivity of design alternatives to performance aspects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this research provides the basis for the development of a software tool to support conceptual design of buildings.
the use of uncertainty propagation and sensitivity techniques is a promising approach to support the early design process.
simulation tools with features to address uncertainties and sensitivies can support conceptual design by reducing the number of necessary iterations and the risk of suboptimal solutions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to show that BPS tools can support conceptual design, if the tools are adapted and extended to fit the specific needs of conceptual design.
the application of simulation tools to support design decision making in conceptual design has a significant potential to increase the quality and efficiency of the design process.
we developed an integrated approach to support decision making during conceptual design by using building performance simulation and uncertainty propagation and sensitivity analyses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
simulation tools that are designed to address the specific needs of the conceptual design stage can be used to generate value.
the early use of BPS tools can be beneficial to the conceptual design process and that the use of uncertainty propagation and sensitivity tools is a promising approach.
BPS tools are capable to provide support to conceptual design.
